newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Canada firms, Citibank eye Brazil's Band B selloff.
newsitem.headline: Canada firms, Citibank eye Brazil's Band B selloff.

text.p: Canada's Telesystems, Bell Canada and Citicorp's Citibank are negotiating with a local group to compete in the privatization of Brazil's Band B cellular services, an official said.
"There is no document signed yet. We are still finalizing discussions," said Evandro Oliveira, executive superintendent of Banco do Brasil's Capital Markets and Investments.

A group made up of local banks Banco do Brasil; Opportunity; Bozano, Simonsen and eight local pension funds is still talking to with those foreign firms and other international operators to form a giant consortium, he said.
"We have only small details to work out," he said. "We don't have a deadline but we are anxious to get going (so) everything will probably be completed within two weeks," Oliveira said.

He declined to say what other foreign firms the local group is negotiating with. But under any agreement, the Brazilian partners would own a 51 percent stake while foreigners would be operating partners and control up to 49 percent, he added.
The Band B selloff, slated to begin next year, will be the start of the privatization of Brazil's mammoth telecoms sector.
So far, with demand for cellular phone lines nationwide set to balloon ten-fold to 15 million lines by 2000, more than a dozen groups are keen to take part in the Band B frequency selloff.
